title: A Vector for the Archive
premise: Felix Amberdale, navigator of the colony ship Meridian, keeps a secret log documenting the slow collapse of the settlement on Vesper's Reach—and the illegal memory backups stored in the hold, copies of colonists who believe themselves original. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew aged backward by relativistic anomaly, Felix realizes the returning fleet will demand the backups be activated to repopulate a dying world, while the colonial council wants them destroyed to protect their claim to being the 'real' people. Falling in love with Ilsa Vane, the returned ship's de-aged archivist who carries proof that the backups are legally the true heirs, Felix must falsify navigation records to keep the two fleets from open war. In the end, he confesses everything, choosing truth over both duty and safety, and the colonists vote to wake the backups as siblings rather than replacements—Felix among them, having discovered his own backup sleeps in the hold.
about_author: Astrid Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime cartographer who turned to science fiction after two decades charting coastlines that no longer exist. She writes about people who keep records, and what records do to the people keeping them.

chapters.title: The Hold Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Felix, in first-person log entries, introduces the dying colony of Vesper's Reach and his nightly visits to the sealed backup vault in Meridian's hold, where 4,000 sleeping copies hum in cold storage. He tells no one—not even his lover, Councilor Dree. The emotional beat is quiet complicity: he tends the backups like graves, or like children.

chapters.title: Salt in the Reactors
chapters.summary: The colony's failing infrastructure claims its first domed town; Felix navigates supply runs and watches Dree vote to ration medicine rather than admit collapse. His log grows more confessional. Beat: the widening gap between official optimism and recorded truth, and Felix's guilt at being the only honest witness.

chapters.title: A Ship Younger Than Its Log
chapters.summary: The deep-space vessel Perihelion returns after forty years—its crew biologically aged backward, led by archivist Ilsa Vane, who looks nineteen but remembers decades. She requests access to colonial archives and immediately notices discrepancies in Felix's navigation records. Beat: uncanny wonder shadowed by the threat of being seen through.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the Perihelion's discovery: the time anomaly proves the backups were always part of the founding contract—the returnees' legal charter names the sleeping copies as heirs to the colony. She asks Felix, as navigator, to verify the hold's contents. Beat: attraction kindling between Felix and Ilsa against his better judgment.

chapters.title: The Council of Originals
chapters.summary: Dree and the council learn of the charter clause and move secretly to destroy the backups, framing it as biosecurity. Felix, caught between his lover and his conscience, begins altering flight logs to delay the council's inspection of the hold. Beat: love against duty sharpens into active deception.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: The Perihelion's escort fleet arrives in orbit demanding the backups be activated per charter; the council mobilizes colonial militia. Felix feeds both sides falsified coordinates, buying days. Ilsa suspects him and confronts him; he half-confesses. Beat: the lie becomes load-bearing, and Felix feels himself thinning under it.

chapters.title: The Backup Named Felix
chapters.summary: Searching the vault manifest to forge an inventory, Felix finds his own name—backup F. Amberdale, seeded before launch. He realizes he may be the copy, not the original, and that his entire identity rests on a record he alone keeps. Beat: identity crisis; the archive turns inward and devours its keeper.

chapters.title: Dree's Hand on the Switch
chapters.summary: Dree discovers Felix's forged logs and, heartbroken, gives the council the real route to the vault. Militia breaches the hold as the orbital fleet threatens bombardment. Ilsa chooses Felix over her fleet's ultimatum, transmitting the charter publicly. Beat: betrayal, then the climax ignites—both fleets converge on the vault.

chapters.title: Confession at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Climax: Felix broadcasts his full log—every death, every forgery, every backup—to both fleets, standing between militia guns and the vault doors. He admits he doesn't know if he's original or copy, and argues neither fact should decide who lives. The firing stops; the fleets stand down long enough to talk. Beat: truth as the only disarmament.

chapters.title: Siblings, Not Replacements
chapters.summary: Resolution: a joint assembly votes to wake the backups as legal siblings with shared inheritance; the first waking is Felix's own double, who greets him without rancor. Dree leaves on the Perihelion; Ilsa stays. Felix ends the log, handing authorship to the newly woken. Beat: inheritance redefined—identity as something shared forward, not defended.
